rows.31:7150:
Late one night, her house caught fire.
Her family escaped unharmed, but the house burned to the ground.
Naturally, the painting that had been on her bed burned with it.
The Shimizus, burned out of their home, moved away, saying they would go to stay with relatives.{p}
rows.31:7430:
Instead, a rumor started that it would begin sobbing late at night.
I'm sure she was lonely.
But everyone was so frightened of it that in the end they took the painting down.
rows.31:7b7c:
One day, her painting, which should have been in the art room, suddenly vanished.
Everyone searched, but they couldn't find it, so they decided to ask the uncle, just in case.{p}
rows.31:876c:
...Oh my, you look rather angry.
Is it because I invited you to the art room, where that painting is, without telling you any of this?
Heh heh... Don't tell me you're only now getting scared?
Well then, I'll end my story here.
Who's next?{p}
rows.31:8fc0:
The door closed.
Now that I was alone, the club room, which should have felt cramped, seemed strangely vast.
It seemed as if something might be lurking in the dim corners of the room, and {f:I|I} couldn't help glancing all around.
rows.31:9488:
To me it's just an ordinary painting, but I wonder what it looks like to you.
Maybe you're seeing the face she had when she was killed.
If so, {a}{f:|}, you might just be the fifth one, don't you think?
...I'm a little curious about the face you saw, but I think I'd rather not ask after all.
You may not believe it, but I scare easily.{p}
rows.31:9890:
What's with that dismissive attitude?
I'm asking you something, so would you answer me properly?{p}
